what: Dev-only sweep that chooses the dacl10k v2a ONNX segmenter's look profile (drishyam.agent.PROFILES), then compares v2a at that profile with v1 at its own and with the classical engine. Never a held-out set. Pre-registration stub: the rule and the grid below were committed before any v2a sweep row was run or read; the rows, the decision and the comparison are added after.
costs: fixed: job_ops p50 ms per call from results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a/micro.json (v2a timed on this Mac, 1 cv2 thread, load 7.9 at start, 7.8 at end); the baselines are charged the same table; governor overrides off (harness.run_drishyam)

variants.ref: min_view 0.3, absorb off: v1's profile values (onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx), the reference, listed first
variants.mv0: min_view 0, absorb off: any level (L0 the finest everywhere)
variants.mv15: min_view 0.15, absorb off: L1 the finest on the 3648- to 6000-px photos, L0 on the 2048- to 2856-px ones
variants.mv25: min_view 0.25, absorb off: v1's runner-up (L2 the finest on 3648- to 6000-px photos, L0 on 2048-px ones)
variants.old: min_view 0, absorb on: the classical-v1 values (the agent before profiles)

rule: Stated before any v2a sweep row was run. Reference: ref (v1's values), listed first in every run, so every candidate is paired with it on the same images and the same cost table. A candidate replaces ref only if, at the 30 % cap, (1) its recall is higher than ref's on synth_dev AND on CODEBRIM dev100, each counted only when the paired 95 % bootstrap CI of its recall ratio to ref (vs_ref_ci) lies wholly above 1; and (2) it has no more false alarms on the clean split at the 30 % cap, a harm counted by the same standard: the paired 95 % CI of its boxes-per-photo difference to ref lies wholly above 0, or the CI of the difference in the share of photos with any box (images_with_any_vs_ref_ci) lies wholly above 0. A CI that touches or crosses no change counts as no change, for a gain and for a harm alike. If several candidates pass, the one whose lower vs_ref_ci bound, taken as the smaller of the two splits, is higher. If none passes, v2a gets v1's values (min_view 0.3, absorb off). Everything else (the 1.0 cap, IoU-only recall, boxes on the recall splits, critical boxes, the ratios to L0 tiling and the downscale) is reported, not part of the rule.
command: python -m evals.dev_sweep <clean|synth_dev|real> 0.3,1.0 "<variants>" --workers 4 --baselines --micro-arm local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a --codebrim <the main checkout's data/codebrim, read-only> --out <f> --dump <f>, with DRISHYAM_ONNX=models/drishyam_dacl10k_v2a.onnx and DRISHYAM_ONNX_FP16 beside it and PYTHONPATH the worktree (runs/v2a/sweep.sh, the load before and after in each run's log); the comparison runs the same command with the variant "head=" (no knob: the profile by name), v1 with --micro-arm local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime, the classical engine (no DRISHYAM_ONNX) with local-macos-x86; v1 on its committed table and the head check without --baselines
decision: no candidate passed the rule: onnx:drishyam_dacl10k_v2a.onnx gets min_view 0.3, absorb False (v1's values)

chosen.meaning: onnx:drishyam_dacl10k_v2a.onnx resolves to these values only with the weights above (agent.WEIGHTS); the same file name with other weights gets classical-v1. min_view 0.3 makes L2 the finest level on CODEBRIM's 3648- to 6000-px photos and L1 on 2048-px ones (synth_dev, clean)

notes: grid rows set min_view and absorb explicitly, so their jobs record profile classical-v1 (the name had no PROFILES entry when they ran, and PROFILES holds no other knob); head rows record the model's own profile (per_image.<row>.profiles, from each job)

mv0, mv15 and mv25 are one policy on the 2048-px synth_dev and clean photos (L0 the finest for all three: L0 of a 2048-px photo spans 0.25 of its side), so their rows there match except chance_recall, whose random boxes are seeded by the row name

pairs and every _ci: paired 95 % bootstrap intervals over images (1000 resamples, seed 0, evals.harness.boot_ci); within a run against ref (vs_ref_ci), across runs image by image (the image ids of every run are asserted equal, and every run's dataset sha256 equals results/dev/onnx_profile_sweep.json's)
clean false alarms: on the clean split every box is a false alarm; the rule reads the boxes-per-photo difference (defined when ref has no box, unlike a ratio) and the share of photos with any box

machine load: files.<run>.load (the 1-min load at the run's start and end, and its min / median / max over one sample a minute); another job (other worktrees' eval workers) shared the machine throughout, and this work ran at most 4 worker processes. The fixed cost table makes the rows independent of the load; only the micro timings depend on it (latency)

boxes are per-component boxes (the harness's primary convention for every policy); critical_per_image counts boxes of a critical class and size (findings.is_critical), the ones the human gate would hold
